title: Route-level A/B testing framework — kickoff notes (working doc)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture kickoff discussion + open questions for Route-level A/B testing (“Route Experiments”) as an extension of Console → Rollouts.
- This is a working doc. Expect partial decisions + TODOs.

Date/time
- 2025-01-09 (kickoff) + async follow-ups through 2025-01-16

Attendees
- Product: Marissa Cole
- Eng (Console & Tooling): Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams
- Platform Control Plane / Policy Engine: Ethan Park, Jordan Lee
- Telemetry/Analytics: Logan Wright
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher
- Design: Tessa Morgan

Problem statement (why now)
- Customers (and internal teams) want to safely compare model variants (and routing/prompt changes) with deterministic user assignment and first-class measurement.
- Today: canary rollouts exist, but A/B testing is ad-hoc (manual header-based overrides, external dashboards, inconsistent attribution).
- We need a supported “experiment at routing layer” primitive with:
  - deterministic bucketing + traffic splits
  - attribution schema for latency/cost/errors (and optionally quality/evals)
  - safe operational controls (guardrails, rollback triggers, audit logging)
  - Console workflow + visibility

Goals (v1 / beta)
1) Control plane experience (create/manage experiments)
- Define experiment model at route level:
  - route selector (route_id / endpoint)
  - variants (target policies/model versions)
  - allocation splits (A/B/n)
  - eligibility rules (account, region, headers/attributes where applicable)
  - start/stop state machine (draft → running → stopped)
- Validation that prevents common footguns (see “Edge cases / validation” section).
- Audit log coverage for lifecycle + config changes.

2) Data plane deterministic assignment
- Request routing evaluates experiment eligibility on each request.
- Deterministic assignment to variant based on a stickiness key with clearly defined precedence.
- Stickiness must be stable across:
  - retries (esp. streaming)
  - router restarts
  - regions (within constraints)
- Precedence rules clarified between experiments and existing rollout mechanisms (canary/fallback).

3) Telemetry + attribution + dashboards
- Canonical attribution dimensions: {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id} + core dims already in pipeline (model_id, region, account_id tier, etc. per cardinality rules).
- Standard metrics by variant:
  - latency p50/p95/p99
  - error rate (by error class where possible)
  - throughput (rps) and tokens/sec
  - cost per request + cost per 1K output tokens (plus “GPU time proxy” if needed)
- Drop-rate tracking: % of requests in experiment that fail to emit attribution fields.

4) Safety and operability
- Guardrails: define thresholds + evaluate continuously, with:
  - soft-stop behavior in initial beta (alert + mark degraded + show banner)
  - optional hard-stop for severe regressions (behind kill switch; SRE sign-off)
- Blast radius controls:
  - max % traffic cap per experiment by default (configurable by RBAC role)
  - restrictions on number of concurrent experiments per route (decision pending)
- Runbooks for:
  - skew detection
  - attribution drop
  - config propagation lag

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for GA per kickoff)
- Full statistical significance engine (we will show deltas + guardrail status; no p-values / power calcs for GA).
- Customer-managed arbitrary custom metric ingestion.
- Multi-region rebalancing beyond deterministic bucketing (no “global traffic optimization” in v1).
- Fully automated “choose winner and roll forward” workflow.

Success metrics (for beta/GA gate)
- Functional correctness
  - Determinism: same request inputs → same variant assignment (within a config version).
  - Split accuracy: observed distribution matches configured split within expected error bounds.
  - Attribution completeness: <0.5% attribution drop rate for supported request types (streaming/non-streaming).
- Product value
  - Design partners can create an experiment in Console and get variant metrics within expected freshness window.
  - Support/SRE can debug skew or missing attribution with documented steps and a debug endpoint.
- Operational safety
  - Guardrail alerts fire with acceptable precision (avoid false positives that cause churn).
  - Propagation lag stays within SLOs (TBD; see SLO section).

Decisions made (so far)
1) Deterministic bucketing approach
- Use hashing-based bucketing (see ADR-047).
- Bucket input = stable stickiness key (see open question below) + experiment_id + config version salt.
- Assignment is computed at router/policy evaluation time.

2) Telemetry schema direction
- Adopt a canonical experiment attribution schema (see ADR-048).
- Emit experiment_id + variant_id into request context and OTel spans.
- Keep tagging strategy conservative to limit cardinality; prefer aggregation jobs/tables for Console queries.

3) Initial guardrail semantics
- Beta: soft-stop only (alert + degrade status + recommended action). Hard-stop requires explicit enablement + kill switch + SRE review.

Open questions (need answers before we call Phase 1 “done”)
A) Stickiness key choice + precedence
- What key do we use for deterministic assignment?
  - Options discussed:
    1) customer-provided explicit “experiment_sticky_key” header/field (best determinism, but requires adoption)
    2) customer_id / account_id (good for B2B; but may not represent end-user)
    3) end_user_id (if provided by customer; often missing)
    4) session_id / device_id (higher entropy, but customers may not have stable session semantics)
    5) fallback to request_id (bad: defeats stickiness; creates high churn)
- Proposed precedence (tentative):
  1) explicit sticky_key provided in request (SDK-supported)
  2) end_user_id (if provided)
  3) customer/account id
  4) (last resort) hashed IP + user agent (privacy + instability concerns; likely NOT acceptable for many customers)
- Action needed: finalize precedence + define behavior when missing (e.g., block experiment start unless key coverage >X%? or allow but warn in Console and clamp max traffic?).

B) Multi-tenant isolation
- If multiple experiments exist, how do we prevent one tenant’s config from impacting another (especially on shared routing infra)?
  - Strict scoping in policy evaluation by account_id.
  - Ensure config caching keys include tenant scope and are not accidentally “global.”
- Do we allow “org-wide experiments” that apply to multiple accounts (internal Redwood use) vs customer-only scope?
  - Proposed: support internal override behind separate RBAC flag; keep customer experiments strictly scoped.

C) Overlapping experiments (same route)
- Block overlapping experiments by default?
  - Pros: avoids combinatorial interactions and attribution confusion.
  - Cons: power users may want stacked experiments (e.g., model A/B and prompt A/B simultaneously).
- Alternative: allow overlaps with explicit priority order and an “experiment layer” concept.
- Tentative direction: for v1, block overlaps on the same route unless an internal feature flag is enabled.
- Need UX copy: Console should explain why you can’t start experiment B while experiment A is running on same route.

D) Interactions with existing Rollouts: canary + fallback
- What is the evaluation order?
  - If a route is in canary rollout AND an experiment is running, which decides the variant?
- Tentative direction from discussion: apply experiment selection before fallback evaluation, but ensure fallback still applies if the selected variant is unhealthy/unavailable.
- Need explicit precedence rules documented for customers.

E) Metrics freshness + results computation ownership
- What is the expected freshness of results in Console?
  - Real-time per-request metrics are expensive; we likely rely on rollups.
- Ownership boundary:
  - Console backend provides results API.
  - Telemetry pipeline owns aggregation datasets/tables.
  - Platform services own emitting correct attribution.
- Define “results API” contract early to prevent late-stage rework.

F) Cardinality controls
- How many variants max per experiment?
  - Tentative: cap at 5 variants for GA; configurable internally.
- Which dimensions are allowed in metric tagging vs offline aggregation?
  - Default tags: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id (normalized), region.
  - Avoid tagging: customer_id directly on high-volume metrics.
- Need “route_id normalization” policy (template path vs raw path) to avoid explosion.

G) Guardrail defaults
- Defaults proposed for beta (very tentative; needs SRE sign-off):
  - p99 latency regression > +20% vs control for 10 minutes → degrade
  - error rate regression > +0.5% absolute for 10 minutes → degrade
  - cost per 1K output tokens > +15% vs control for 30 minutes → degrade
- Need to ensure guardrails don’t flap during low traffic; incorporate minimum sample thresholds.

Risks / watch-outs
1) Missing attribution (especially streaming + retries)
- Highest risk to “trust in results.”
- Mitigation:
  - propagate experiment context through retries
  - add attribution drop-rate metric + alert
  - integration tests for streaming and retry paths

2) Allocation skew (low entropy or missing stickiness key)
- Risk: customers see “50/50” config but traffic is 80/20.
- Mitigation:
  - console validation: show key coverage estimate and warn/block start
  - debug endpoint to explain assignment inputs
  - automatic skew detection alert

3) Config propagation lag
- Risk: inconsistent assignment across routers/regions, confusing customers (“variant changed mid-session”).
- Mitigation:
  - clear staleness bounds, versioned configs
  - propagation lag metric + alert
  - safe fallback behavior when config missing (e.g., route to control)

4) Metrics cost blow-ups
- Extra dimensions can balloon metric series and increase infra spend.
- Mitigation:
  - strict tag set
  - sampling for high-cardinality expansions
  - prefer offline rollups for drill-downs

5) UX complexity
- Experiments are inherently complex; we need a guided flow with safe defaults and clear “what happens” explanations.
- Avoid shipping a UI that makes wrong setups easy.

Architecture sketch (very rough)
- Experiment Service (control plane)
  - Stores experiment configs + versions
  - Validates and emits audit events
  - Exposes APIs for Console
- Policy Engine / Router (data plane)
  - Fetches config via cached distribution
  - Evaluates eligibility + deterministic bucketing
  - Writes {experiment_id, variant_id} into request context
- Telemetry
  - OTel span tags + event schema updates
  - Aggregation jobs to produce per-variant metrics
- Console
  - Creation wizard → review → start
  - Experiment list/detail pages
  - Results dashboard with deltas + guardrail state
  - Audit/change history panel

Initial task breakdown (proposed)
Phase 0 (PRD + design + ADR alignment)
- [Marissa] Draft PRD and confirm GA scope/non-goals.
- [Jordan/Jada] Finalize ADR-047 details: hashing inputs, salt/versioning.
- [Logan] Finalize ADR-048 metric dimensions and cardinality rules.
- [Tessa] UX wireframes for creation flow + results dashboard.

Phase 1 (core backend + router behind flag)
Control plane
- Implement experiment config schema + validation.
- API endpoints: create/update/start/stop; list; get detail.
- Audit events for lifecycle operations.

Data plane
- Policy evaluation: apply experiments at route level with deterministic assignment.
- Precedence w/ fallback policies.
- Config caching and safe default if config unavailable.

Telemetry
- Plumb experiment_id/variant_id through request context.
- Emit OTel tags + minimal metrics.

Phase 2 (Console UI + analytics + eval hook)
- Console creation wizard + list/detail pages behind feature flag.
- Results dashboard using aggregated tables.
- Add “debug this assignment” view (internal-only at first) or at least link to support.
- Evals hook: accept variant tag in eval outputs and show a “quality” tile (if available).

Phase 3 (hardening + GA)
- SLOs + dashboards + alerts + runbooks.
- RBAC and permissioning polish (who can start/stop, who can view results).
- Backfill/migration plan for schema changes.
- Support readiness checklist + docs.

Action items (as of 2025-01-16)
- Dylan: Write up stickiness key proposal + required customer contract (header/SDK field). Deadline: 2025-01-21.
- Jordan + Jada: Propose final precedence rules + behavior when key missing. Deadline: 2025-01-22.
- Chloe: Draft control plane API shapes for create/start/stop + error semantics; share for review. Deadline: 2025-01-23.
- Logan: Define initial attribution drop-rate metric and where it’s computed. Deadline: 2025-01-23.
- Sean: Provide recommended initial guardrail defaults + minimum sample thresholds; define beta alert severities. Deadline: 2025-01-24.
- Tessa: Provide v1 UX for “overlapping experiments blocked” and guardrail warning states. Deadline: 2025-01-24.

Notes / discussion snippets (raw)
- “We should not pretend we do stats sig in GA. Deltas + guardrails is already high value.”
- “If we allow missing sticky key, we need to clamp traffic % hard. Otherwise skew will look like a bug.”
- “Attribution drop rate is a first-class SLO; otherwise customers will distrust the dashboard.”
- “Audit logging is table-stakes for enterprise; include change diff summary (what fields changed).”

Parking lot (later)
- Experiment templates (e.g., ‘compare model versions’ preset).
- Automatic winner selection and rollout.
- Customer custom metrics.
- Advanced segmentation in Console (geo/device) beyond what we can do safely with cardinality.
